clue.text: Airgun?

parts.note: read as a gun powered by the air you breathe out: a tube through which darts are puffed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Airgun' suggests a pellet rifle; the question mark asks you to take it as a weapon driven by the shooter's own breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube for shooting darts by breath is a weapon fired by air from the lungs.

clue.text: from Serbia

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads only 'from Serbia (6)': the definition and anagram indicator are missing (BRAISE is an anagram of SERBIA), and no reprint or search gives the missing words.

clue.text: Move furtively below circle of bones

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece placed below comes after the other one

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O
to steal is to creep or move furtively

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks beneath a ring of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is an adjective meaning relating to or resembling bone.

clue.text: Pounding implement made from soft malleable steel

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: something malleable can be bent into new shapes, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tool for pounding has been forged from a soft, workable steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'malleable' looks like a description of the metal but signals rearranging STEEL into ESTLE, after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is the club-shaped tool used to crush substances in a mortar.

clue.text: Landing stage for cruisers

parts.note: read as a stop on a cruise ship's itinerary where passengers go ashore, not a jetty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing stage' suggests a pier; read it as a stage of the journey where cruise passengers land.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour where a ship stops during a voyage is one of its scheduled stops.

clue.text: Witty remark about New Mexico's luggage accommodation

indicators.note: the word for luggage space goes round the other piece, encircling it

parts.note: a car's boot is its luggage compartment (US trunk)
NM is the postal abbreviation for New Mexico

explanation.surface: A clever quip concerning where New Mexico stores its luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOT is the British word for a car's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon mot is a clever, well-turned saying, French for good word.

clue.text: Easily eclipse Oxford University girl initially entering Trinity College

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the words Trinity and College are taken

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: An Oxford student easily outshines a young woman getting into Trinity College.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' joins the girl to the college letters she follows; TC comes from the first letters of Trinity College.
explanation.definitionFit: To outclass rivals is to surpass them by a wide margin, to put them in the shade.

clue.text: Measurement's affected climate either side of river

definitions.note: possessive used for the adjective: pertaining to measurement

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit on both sides of the river letter, surrounding it
affected means altered or disturbed, so the letters of climate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A measurement has been changed by a climate found on both banks of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges CLIMATE into METICAL, which goes either side of R.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrical means relating to measurement, as well as to poetic metre.

clue.text: Relatively fashionable object seen in German city

indicators.note: one piece is found sitting inside the other

parts.note: Trier is an old city in western Germany
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Something trendy is spotted in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatively, i.e. comparatively, fashionable is the comparative form, more modish.

clue.text: Playing sitar, attempt to show skill

indicators.note: playing about with the word sitar mixes up its letters

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A musician tries the sitar to display their talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' looks like performing on the instrument, but it signals an anagram of SITAR, giving ARTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill or craftsmanship.

clue.text: Figure from Uruguay surrounded by ceremonial dignity

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, which encloses it

parts.note: lying in state or arriving in state means with ceremonial pomp
U is the international vehicle code for Uruguay

explanation.surface: A dignitary from Uruguay is honoured with great ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure.

clue.text: Cat follows tailless old horse

indicators.note: the cat word comes after the other piece
the final letter of the word for old is cut off

parts.note: stale means old, no longer fresh
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat chases an elderly horse that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' drops the last letter of STALE, leaving STAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse.

clue.text: Joined in a student song

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate
a lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: Someone joined in as a student sang.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means united or connected, as partners are.

clue.text: Franchise holders in Hanover, typically

definitions.meaning: the people who hold the franchise, i.e. the right to vote
Hanover was a German state ruled by a prince-elector, an example of such a territory

explanation.surface: Voting rights holders in the city of Hanover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The rulers of some Holy Roman Empire states, including Hanover, elected the emperor, and their territories had this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of voters takes this name, as did the domain of a German prince-elector.

clue.text: Fruity item producing unseemly cackles in English church

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: unseemly means improper or disordered, so the letters of cackles are jumbled

explanation.surface: Unseemly cackling breaks out in an English church over a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eccles cake is a British currant pastry named after a Lancashire town. 'unseemly' looks like a comment on the noise but signals the anagram; 'in' puts it inside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: This round pastry from Lancashire is stuffed with currants, making it a fruit-filled bake.

clue.text: Turn over US state to find amino-compound

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, is written at the foot of a page
Maine is a state in the north-eastern United States

explanation.surface: Flip a page about an American state to discover a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over' looks like a reversal instruction but is the abbreviation PTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are nitrogen compounds produced when protein decays, once blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Unfortunate results of foot in mouth actions?

definitions.text: Unfortunate results of foot in mouth actions?

parts.words: Unfortunate results of foot in mouth actions?
parts.note: read 'foot in mouth' as a footballer's self-defeating kick and 'mouth' as the goalmouth, not a social gaffe

explanation.walkthrough: 'foot in mouth' suggests saying something tactless; in football, a foot putting the ball into your own goalmouth scores against your side.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicking the ball into your own team's net scores for the opposition, a mistake that hurts yourself.

clue.text: Tip when playing guitar, extremely twangy

indicators.note: playing around with the word guitar rearranges its letters
only the outermost letters, first and last, of twangy are used

explanation.surface: A busker gets a tip for twangy guitar music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when playing' signals an anagram of GUITAR (GRATUI); 'extremely twangy' gives TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratuity is a sum given for service, like a waiter's tip.

clue.text: High-rise building, fatal spot for Tudor queens?

definitions.meaning: a tall residential building of many storeys
the executioner's block at the Tower of London, where Anne Boleyn and Catherine Howard were beheaded

explanation.surface: A skyscraper is where Tudor queens met their end.
explanation.walkthrough: Two of Henry VIII's queens were beheaded at the Tower of London, the royal fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall apartment building has this name; split, it is the chopping block at the Tower.

clue.text: European gets part-exchange for feeding-trough

indicators.note: the two parts of the word swap places, exchanging positions

parts.note: a German is a European

explanation.surface: A European trades in part of something for a cattle trough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part-exchange' usually means trading in an old item; here GER and MAN swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is a long open box from which horses or cattle eat.

clue.text: Left surrounded by endless rubbish? Not at all

indicators.note: the left letter is enclosed within the other piece
the last letter of the rubbish word is dropped

parts.note: litter is rubbish dropped in public

explanation.surface: Left behind amid unending junk? Absolutely not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts LITTER to LITTE, and L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, as in little did they know, it means not in the least.

clue.text: Persian king accepts power in island

indicators.note: the king's name takes in another letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian Empire
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A Persian ruler takes power on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a Mediterranean island nation.

clue.text: Wonderful youth leader was allowed to go ahead

indicators.note: the permission word goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: might is the past tense of may, meaning was permitted

indicators.note: the leader of youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: A youth leader was given permission to proceed with something marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'youth leader' looks like a person in charge of young people but is the first letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, mighty means great or impressive, as in a mighty effort.

clue.text: Sum Italy squandered on drink

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means coming after

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: squandered means wasted or scattered, so the letters of Italy are jumbled

explanation.surface: Italy has wasted a fortune on alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squandered' looks like money wasted on drink, but it signals that the country's letters are jumbled; a tot is a small British measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Totality means the whole amount, the total.

clue.text: Appeal by girl mostly having right inclination?

definitions.note: adjective describing type that slopes to the right

parts.note: it is sex appeal, as in the 1920s it girl

indicators.note: most of the name is used, dropping its final letter

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's charm suggests she leans the right way politically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right inclination' hints at conservative views; it means slanting rightward like sloped type.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes upward to the right.

clue.text: Family member beaten up by the guard

indicators.note: beaten up means assaulted or knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative is assaulted by the security guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' signals an anagram of THE GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child, a member of a household.

clue.text: Literary productions by Society, for instance, in El Salvador

indicators.note: the society and example words are placed within the country code

parts.note: ES is the international vehicle code for El Salvador
say means for example

explanation.surface: Writings published by a society in El Salvador, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Essays are short pieces of prose writing on a subject.

clue.text: Unrivalled, like the green benches at Westminster

definitions.text: like the green benches at Westminster
definitions.meaning: the green benches are in the House of Commons, where no members of the House of Lords sit

explanation.surface: Unmatched, just like the seating in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament the Commons has green benches and the Lords red ones, so the green benches lack members of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Without equal is the plain meaning; split, it means lacking lords, as Commons seats are.
